newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes lower on cash prospects.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes lower on cash prospects.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower on increased farm movement and prospects for additional selling soon amid better weather outlooks for the U.S. Upper Midwest, traders said.
"Some of the selling was tied to country movement and with weather clearing it should bring in more farmer movement," a trader said.

Atwood Peavy was the key seller of four million bushels of March and two million May, traders said. Cargill Investor Services and Benson Quinn each bought two million March and Continental Grain bought one million March, the traders said.
"There was good country movement and that's why the front end has taken a hit," a trader said.

Traders said the wheat market also was pressed by slack export sales of U.S. wheat, corn/wheat and soybean wheat spreading, and on diminished fears about winterkill in the U.S. winter wheat growing region.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 2-3/4 to nine cents per bushel lower, with March down nine at $3.85-1/4.
